# SmartMesh WirelessHART Solutions

Now available with breakthrough Eterna™ SoC technology, SmartMesh® WirelessHART products are designed for the harshest industrial environments, where low power, reliability, resilience, and scalability are key, making them well-suited for WirelessHART-specific designs.
SmartMesh WirelessHART complies with the WirelessHART (IEC 62591) standard and offers the lowest power consumption in its class. Analog Devices’ SmartMesh team pioneered the Time Synchronized Mesh Protocol that underpins the WirelessHART standard, and SmartMesh WirelessHART products have been deployed with most of the Fortune 500 companies that make WirelessHART compliant sensor networking products for industrial applications.

Show More Image: Arrow image

## Value and Benefits

  * Lower System Costs: WirelessHART solutions reduce maintenance and eliminate cables for lower infrastructure expenses.
  * Improved Efficiency: Monitor and predict material requirements to optimize resource use.
  * Enhanced Safety: Automate processes previously unmanageable with wired solutions for safer operations.

# DC9022A

SmartMesh WirelessHART RF Certified Starter Kit

## Overview

  * Product Details

## Product Details

The DC9022 SmartMesh^{®}WirelessHART RF Certified Starter Kit provides all the tools for evaluating SmartMesh network performance for your application needs, including high reliability, ultralow power, scalability and ease of installation. This accelerates device integration and application development.

The DC9022 Starter Kit includes five motes or nodes (DC9018A-C) to enable users to quickly deploy a multi-hop mesh network in the RF environment for your specific application. The software graphical user interface (GUI) allows you to quickly see the mesh network form, as well as key performance statistics, such as data reliability and latency.

The DC9018A-C Evaluation/Development Mote Modules feature easy-to-probe signal pins. In addition, the starter kit provides access to both manager and mote software application programming interfaces (APIs) to enable application software development.

The DC9022 Starter Kit operates in the 2.4000GHz to 2.4835GHz international license-free frequency band and includes RF intentional radiator certifications for Japan, as well as the United States, Canada and Europe. Starter kits and demo boards are for evaluation purposes only. It remains the user’s responsibility to verify proper and reliable operation in the actual end application.

The SmartMesh WirelessHART Starter Kit – includes the following items:

  * One Packaged Manager (LTP5903CEN-WHRB)
  * Five Evaluation / Development Motes (DC9018A-C)
  * One Eterna Interface Card (DC9006), which includes a DC9004 adapter card
  * Additional CR2032 batteries
  * Cables

L1718@P22: Mote API Guide for details on the disconnect and reset
L1719@P22: commands. Eterna includes a soft brown-out monitor that
L1720@P22: fully protects the flash from corruption in the event that
L1721@P22: power is removed while writing to flash. Integrated flash
L1722@P22: supervisory functionality, in conjunction with a fault tolerant
L1723@P22: file system, yields a robust nonvolatile storage solution.
L1724@P22: Precision Timing
L1725@P22: Eterna’s unique low power dedicated timing hardware and
L1726@P22: timing algorithms provides a significant improvement over
L1727@P22: competing 802.15.4 product offerings. This functionality
L1728@P22: provides timing precision two to three orders of magnitude
L1729@P22: better than any other low-power solution available at the
L1730@P22: time of publication. Improved timing accuracy allows motes
L1731@P22: to minimize the amount of radio listening time required
L1732@P22: to ensure packet reception thereby lowering even further
L1733@P22: the power consumed by SmartMesh networks. Eterna’s
L1734@P22: patented timing hardware and timing algorithms provide
L1735@P22: superior performance over rapid temperature changes,
L1736@P22: further differentiating Eterna’s reliability when compared
L1737@P22: with other wireless products. In addition, precise timing
L1738@P22: enables networks to reduce spectral dead time, increasing
L1739@P22: total network throughput.
L1740@P22: Application Time Synchronization
L1741@P22: In addition to coordinating time slots across the network,
L1742@P22: which is transparent to the user, Eterna’s timing management is used to support two mechanisms to share network
L1743@P22: time. Having an accurate, shared, network-wide time base
L1744@P22: enables events to be accurately time stamped or tasks to
L1745@P22: be performed in a synchronized fashion across a network.
L1746@P22: Eterna will send a time packet through its serial interface
L1747@P22: when one of the following occurs:
L1748@P22: n Eterna receives an API request to read time
L1749@P22: n The TIMEn signal is asserted
L1750@P22: The use of TIMEn has the advantage of being more accurate. The value of the timestamp is captured in hardware
L1751@P22: relative to the rising edge of TIMEn. If an API request is
L1752@P22: used, due to packet processing, the value of the timestamp
L1753@P22: may be captured several milliseconds after receipt of the
L1754@P22: packet. See the TIMEn AC Characteristics section for the
L1755@P22: TIMEn function’s definition and specifications.
L1756@P22: Time References
L1757@P22: Eterna includes three clock sources: an internal relaxation
L1758@P22: oscillator, a low power oscillator designed for a 32.768kHz
L1759@P22: crystal, and the radio reference oscillator designed for a
L1760@P22: 20MHz crystal.
L1761@P22: Relaxation Oscillator
L1762@P22: The relaxation oscillator is the primary clock source for
L1763@P22: Eterna, providing the clock for the CPU, memory subsystems, and all peripherals. The internal relaxation oscillator
L1764@P22: is dynamically calibrated to 7.3728MHz. The internal relaxation oscillator typically starts up in a few μs, providing
L1765@P22: an expedient, low-energy method for duty cycling between
L1766@P22: active and low power states. Quick start-up from the doze
L1767@P22: state, defined in the State Diagram section, allows Eterna to
L1768@P22: wake up and receive data over the UART and SPI interfaces
L1769@P22: by simply detecting activity on the appropriate signals.
L1770@P22: 32.768kHz Crystal
L1771@P22: Once Eterna is powered up and the 32.768kHz crystal
L1772@P22: source has begun oscillating, the 32.768kHz crystal remains operational while in the Active state, and is used as
L1773@P22: the timing basis when in Doze state. See the State Diagram
L1774@P22: section, for a description of Eterna’s operational states.
L1775@P22: 20MHz Crystal
L1776@P22: The 20MHz crystal source provides a frequency reference
L1777@P22: for the radio, and is automatically enabled and disabled by
L1778@P22: Eterna as needed. Eterna requires specific characterized
L1779@P22: 20MHz crystal references. See the the Eterna Integration
L1780@P22: Guide for a complete list of the currently supported 20MHz
L1781@P22-23: crystals.LTC5800-WHM

L1785@P23: Operation
L1786@P23: Radio
L1787@P23: Eterna includes the lowest-power commercially available
L1788@P23: 2.4GHz IEEE 802.15.4 radio by a substantial margin.
L1789@P23: (Please refer to the Radio Specifications section for
L1790@P23: power consumption numbers.). Eterna’s integrated power
L1791@P23: amplifier is calibrated and temperature-compensated to
L1792@P23: consistently provide power at a limit suitable for worldwide
L1793@P23: radio certifications. Additionally, Eterna uniquely includes
L1794@P23: a hardware-based autonomous MAC that handles precise
L1795@P23: sequencing of peripherals, including the transmitter, the
L1796@P23: receiver, and advanced encryption standard (AES) peripherals. The hardware-based autonomous media access
L1797@P23: controller (MAC) minimizes CPU activity, thereby further
L1798@P23: decreasing power consumption.
L1799@P23: UARTs
L1800@P23: The principal network interface is through the application
L1801@P23: programming interface (API) UART. A command-line
L1802@P23: interface (CLI) is also provided for support of test and
L1803@P23: debug functions. Both UARTs sense activity continuously,
L1804@P23: consuming virtually no power until data is transferred and
L1805@P23: automatically returning to their lowest power state after
L1806@P23: the conclusion of a transfer. The definition for packet
L1807@P23: encoding on the API UART interface can be found in the
L1808@P23: SmartMesh WirelessHART Mote API Guide and the CLI
L1809@P23: command definitions can be found in the SmartMesh
L1810@P23: WirelessHART Mote CLI Guide.
L1811@P23: API UART Protocols
L1812@P23: The API UART supports multiple modes with the goal of
L1813@P23: supporting a wide range of companion multipoint control
L1814@P23: units (MCUs) while reducing power consumption of the
L1815@P23: system. As a general rule, higher serial data rates translate
L1816@P23: into lower energy consumption for both endpoints. The API
L1817@P23: UART receive protocol includes two additional signals in addition to UART_RX:UART_RX_RTSn and UART_RX_CTSn.
L1818@P23: The transmit half of the API UART protocol includes two
L1819@P23: additional signals in addition to UART_TX: UART_TX_RTSn
L1820@P23: and UART_TX_CTSn. The two supported protocols are
L1821@P23: referred to as UART Mode 2 and UART Mode 4. Mode
L1822@P23: setting is controlled via the Fuse Table.
L1823@P23: In the Figures accompanying the protocol descriptions,
L1824@P23: signals driven by the companion processor are drawn
L1825@P23: in black and signals driven by Eterna are drawn in blue.
L1826@P23: UART Mode 2
L1827@P23: UART Mode 2 provides the most energy-efficient method
L1828@P23: for operating Eterna’s API UART. UART Mode 2 requires
L1829@P23: the use of all six UART signals, but does not require
L1830@P23: adherence to the minimum inter-packet delay as defined
L1831@P23: in the UART AC Characteristics section. UART Mode 2
L1832@P23: incorporates edge-sensitive flow control, at either 9600
L1833@P23: or 115200 baud. Packets are HDLC encoded with one

L1865@P24: UART Mode 4
L1866@P24: UART Mode 4 incorporates level-sensitive flow control
L1867@P24: on the TX channel and requires no flow control on the
L1868@P24: RX channel, supporting both 9600 and 115200 baud.
L1869@P24: The use of level-sensitive flow control signals enables
L1870@P24: data rates above 9600 baud with the option of using a
L1871@P24: reduced set of the flow control signals; however, Mode
L1872@P24: 4 has specific limitations. First, The use of the RX flow
L1873@P24: control signals (UART_RX_RTSn and UART_RX_CTSn)
L1874@P24: for Mode 4 are optional provided the use is limited to the
L1875@P24: industrial temperature range (–40°C to 85°C); otherwise,
L1876@P24: the flow control is mandatory. If RX flow control signals
L1877@P24: are not used, UART_RX_RTSn should be tied to VSUPPLY
L1878@P24: (inactive) and UART_RX_CTSn should be left unconnected.

L1880@P24: to receive a packet, the companion processor must negate
L1881@P24: UART_TX_CTSn prior to the end of the current packet.
